words: Task 46 will surpass even the tarazu point 'video kaisi ho' level on its full completion, implementing things required.
90 se 99 percent videos L3 ya isse upar ke level ki ho. (kitaab se banne wali kul videos ki baat hai, aur ye koshish ka target hai, blocker nahi)
Scene plan ke hisaab se kisi video ka kuch hissa L2 ka ho sakta hai aur usi mein koi baat L5 se dikhani ho sakti hai; poori video ek level ki bane, ye zaroori nahi.
Content decides the scene plan; the scene plan decides which visual level the video code is made at. BIE itself must be capable up to L5a.

about: The visual level ladder (Task 046, docs/vision/VISUAL_LEVELS.md). The level rule has two stars (Navin, 26 October 2026): A, the chapter or book target (targets.chapter): the share of videos whose main level is L3 or above, 90-99 %, a target to work towards, never a blocker; B, the shot level (targets.shot): every shot carries its own level from shot_levels, chosen from the content and the scene plan; the director picks L3 or above where the content allows and L2 only where a flat drawing shows the point better, with the reason on that shot; no video is blocked because of its level. This file carries no rules; the director (bie/brain/shots.py) and the reports read it.
chain: content → scene plan (one shot per spoken sentence, each with a level) → video code made at that level

chapter.decided: Navin, 26 October 2026: '90 se 99 percent videos L3 ya isse upar ke level ki ho' — kitaab se banne wali kul videos ki baat hai, aur ye koshish ka target hai, blocker nahi.
chapter.measure: the share of a chapter's or book's videos whose main level (the level with most shot-seconds) is L3 or above
chapter.report: every video's main level; videos per main level; the share with main level L3 or above; below the target, the video's name and the reason

shot.decided: Navin, 26 October 2026: 'Scene plan ke hisaab se kisi video ka kuch hissa L2 ka ho sakta hai aur usi mein koi baat L5 se dikhani ho sakti hai; poori video ek level ki bane, ye zaroori nahi.'
shot.rule: the level is per shot, from the content and the scene plan; the director chooses L3 or above where the content allows; L2 only where L2 shows the point better, with the reason written on that shot
shot.report: every video's level mix: which shots at which level (shots, seconds, share per level)
shot.planning_error: a shot at L1 or L5b (outside shot_levels)

pace.decided: Navin, 26 October 2026: the visual-change rate (a block or camera change) is reported per video; target micro biology 3-5 s per change, engineering and physics 10-20 s (one 3D world, the camera moves); VG-01 checks this rate.
pace.measure: seconds per visual change: a shot counts as a change when its block differs from the shot before or its camera moves (not hold); a label or glow moving to another structure is not counted

micro.why: the benchmark pace: 19 changes in 90 s

world.why: one 3D world per topic, the camera moves between its parts

pace.no_band: other families: the rate is reported, no target yet
pace.director: where consecutive clauses would hold the same picture past the band's upper bound, the director adds a camera move (zoom in on the lit structure, orbit, zoom out) so the picture changes within it

levels.name: teacher at a board
levels.means: a person explaining at a board, as in a classroom recording
levels.use: never a BIE output; only for learning how teachers explain (the teacher example bank)

levels.name: clean 2D
levels.means: vector diagrams, draw-on line art, equation cards, slides
levels.use: where a flat drawing is the clearest picture: a vector problem, a circuit, a case card, a definition slide
examples: a vector problem drawn with arrows

levels.name: rich 2D / 2.5D
levels.means: motion graphics, illustrated stills, light 3D, timelines, lit boards, kinetic captions
levels.use: the floor for most teaching shots: equation steps on a lit board, a graph that draws itself, a timeline with nodes, a board that fills, a mnemonic card, a split comparison
examples: equation steps on a lit board

levels.name: stylized 3D
levels.means: one 3D world per topic; the camera moves between its parts; cutaway and exploded views; a process shown with flow
levels.use: engineering, physics apparatus, the earth, machines, orbits
examples: a machine part exploded into its pieces
the earth cut open to its layers
an orbit with the planet moving

levels.name: photoreal micro or machine 3D
levels.means: lighting, depth of field, focus glow, particle motion; cells, molecules, chips, organs
levels.use: the epithelium benchmark level: a lit sheet of cells, particles crossing it, a zoom from the organ to the sheet
examples: a sheet of squamous cells with the top cell glowing
oxygen particles crossing the thin sheet

levels.name: photoreal humans, landscapes, Pixar-grade character acting
levels.means: photoreal people and places, feature-film character animation
levels.use: not made by code; outside BIE's output. A scene plan that asks for L5b is a planning error and fails the check

default_by_kind.note: fallbacks the director uses when a capability has no default_level (it should not happen: every capability names one)
